_comment: What makes a saved collage layout renderable, stated once and asserted by
BOTH implementations (#967, #970).
Every divider drag writes cell geometry straight into the saved override.
CollageRenderer.render then composites those exact cells over the base PNG,
so an impossible layout is not a preview problem: it is what gets exported
and what is written back to events.json. #965 fixed the one drag known to
produce one; this is the rule the SAVE has to satisfy, whatever produced it.
The five ways a layout is not renderable:
under_floor   a cell smaller than MIN_CELL_PX on either axis. The drag
clamps already claim to enforce this, so a saved layout
breaking it means a clamp was wrong or a path skipped one.
off_canvas    a cell that starts before the canvas or ends past it. The
renderer draws it anyway and the photo is cut by the frame.
overlapping   two cells sharing pixels. One photograph is drawn over
another and which one survives depends on cell order.
covers_strip  a cell intersecting the branded centre strip. That band
carries the event title, the org, the venue and the
wordmark, and generate_collage.py:8 says the point of it is
being impossible to crop out when shared. A photo over it
takes the branding off the post.
empty         no cells at all, which is not a layout.
MIN_CELL_PX is 80, the same floor computeCollageDividers clamps drags to.
Stated here rather than restated in the validator so the clamp and the
validator cannot disagree about the floor (L41).
The strip band is given as strip_y and strip_h rather than assumed at a
fixed offset: where it sits depends on how many rows are above it, which
is why generate_collage.infer_strip_y exists. A case with strip_y null has
no strip and only the other four rules apply.
Cells are [photo, x, y, w, h]. Order does not matter to any rule here.

cases.name: an ordinary two row layout with a strip between
a layout with no strip at all
a cell one pixel under the floor
a cell exactly on the floor is fine
a negative height, which is what the strip drag produced
a cell starting before the canvas
a cell ending past the bottom of the canvas
a cell ending exactly at the canvas edge is fine
two cells touching edge to edge do not overlap
the top row grown down over the branded strip
a cell touching the top of the strip but not entering it
a cell overlapping the strip by one pixel
the strip drag at its old ceiling, which produced both faults
no cells is not a layout
